text:
Maya: quick q — we're finalizing per-tier canary scoping and i'm worried about ambiguous fallbacks. if a canary variant is only rolled to enterprise in us-west and that instance fails, do we a) fail enterprise requests, b) spill to the default model in-region, or c) spill to a different region's canary?
Sam: +1 this is a real concern. current smart-routing has regionAffinity > tierPin > variantPreference, but we don't have a clear tiebreaker for canary-only exposures.
Ira: agree. we should define explicit precedence: 1) pinned route (if customer pinned model) 2) same-tier canary exposure 3) regionAffinity 4) global fallback chain. otherwise things get surprising.
Kevin: what about capacity/quotas? if us-west is OOM then regionAffinity will fail. we might want to prefer cross-region spillover for enterprise but not for self-serve. so per-tier policy flags.
Anna: console UX: teams want to see "fallbacks by reason" and per-tier exposure percentages. can we add a telemetry tag for fallback_reason so ops can filter queries that spilled due to capacity vs variant-down vs config?
Maya: yes — add fallback_reason and fallback_target in traces. also emit a routing_decision path like: "pinned->canary->fallback_to_region->fallback_to_global_variant". :eyes:
Sam: quick proposal: extend the API with optional routingHints. sample: 
```json
{"routingHints": {"preferredRegions": ["us-west"], "allowCrossRegionSpill": true, "tierFallbackPolicy": "prefer_lower_latency"}}
```
Ira: that helps but we should avoid making customers set this manually. default server policy should be sane: enterprise: allowCrossRegionSpill=true, premium: prefer same-region but allow variant downgrade, free: prefer cheapest variant within region.
Kevin: also quota impact — if we auto spill to a cheaper quantized variant, we must reflect cost and token accounting correctly (billing tag).ops asked for a billing_tag on fallback events.
ops-bot: runbook reminder — update incident playbook when cross-region spill increases errors.
Anna: regarding rollout UX: if you scope a canary to "enterprise/us-west 10%", the console should show a matrix: tiers x regions x exposure %. also an action to "auto-allow cross-region failover for this canary" with a warning.
Maya: question: during A/B experiments can we keep the same routing semantics? e.g., variant A in us-west enterprise, variant B global? tiebreaker rules must be deterministic for AB scoring. otherwise the exposure percentages are meaningless.
Sam: important. proposal: assign routingPriorityWeight for each variant scoped in rollout config. scoring uses weight + routing constraints. fallback should not change cohort attribution. if request was assigned to cohort A, fallback must still be counted as A (mark fallback_reason=A_fallback).
Ira: telemetry changes needed: route_assigned, route_served, fallback_triggered, fallback_reason. include fields: tier, region_assigned, region_served, variant_assigned, variant_served, queue_wait_ms.
Kevin: low-level: runtime needs a fast tiebreaker function. pseudocode: 
```
if (isPinned) return pinnedVariant; if (variantUpInRegion) return variant; if (tierPolicy.allowCrossRegionSpill && otherRegionHasVariant) return lowestLatencyRegionVariant; if (tierPolicy.allowVariantDowngrade) return fallbackVariantInRegion; return error(503);
```
Anna: UX: add a "what-if" simulator in console to preview routing for a given customer tier + region + percent exposure. that'll help reviewers. :thinking_face:
Maya: decision items: - add routing_decision & fallback_reason tags to traces - add billing_tag on fallback events - default tier policies (enterprise/premium/free) - console matrix and what-if simulator - ensure cohort attribution preserved on fallback
Sam: i'll draft a PR for the API change (routingHints optional) and telemetry schema.
Ira: i'll own runtime tiebreaker implementation and tests. Kevin you own billing tags. Anna you own console changes. Maya i'll coordinate release notes and ops-runbook updates.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-routing-schema-v2 -> staging (CI green). :shipit:
Maya: thanks all. leaving this thread as the decision record. we'll link PRs here when opened.
